findings.claim: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass default evaluated once at class definition, so every AssignmentSource in a process carries the module import time instead of its creation time; the stale value is serialised into every sync_assignee_outbound task.
findings.evidence: Python evaluates dataclass defaults once. Superpowers seat ran a stubbed-timezone repro (two instances 1.5s apart) that raised AssertionError 'queued is frozen at import time'. test_to_dict only asserts queued is not None, so it cannot catch this. Nothing reads queued today. Fix: field(default_factory=timezone.now) or drop the field.
findings.reason: Raised by both correctness seats as Important, with an executed repro; the fix is one line.

findings.claim: The abstract sync_status_outbound gains an `assignment_source` parameter that no caller passes and no implementation reads, so the contract advertises status-sync loop protection that does not exist.
findings.evidence: tasks/sync_status_outbound.py:43 still calls should_sync('outbound_status') with no source. The jira, jira_server, vsts and example implementations do not declare the parameter. ExampleIntegration.sync_status_outbound (example/integration.py:161) has no **kwargs, so it would raise TypeError if a caller ever passed it.
findings.reason: All four seats agree, and reverting the signature removes the misleading contract at no cost.

findings.evidence: Declaration at line 13 of the new test file.

findings.claim: `test_from_dict_empty_array` passes an empty dict, not an array, so the name misdescribes the case.

findings.claim: Test gaps: no test covers deassign with a matching source integration, and no test drives sync_group_assignee_inbound end to end to show the source integration is skipped while a second integration still syncs.
findings.evidence: Only the assign path has a matching-source test (test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration). The ponytail seat noted the same deassign gap but judged it low value because both paths share should_sync.
findings.reason: The deassign path calls should_sync through its own call site, so a cheap test guards against regression. The end-to-end inbound test is the highest-value test for this PR's purpose.

findings.claim: from_dict swallows TypeError/ValueError and returns None, so a malformed payload silently turns off loop protection (fails open into the cycle) with no log or metric. queued is also not type-checked on deserialisation, so it would come back as a str under a JSON serializer.
findings.evidence: assignment_source.py:31-35. should_sync treats None as no source and syncs. Celery uses pickle today (conf/server.py:739), so the type issue is latent.
findings.reason: ponytail: degrades to the pre-patch behaviour and the only producer is to_dict, so there is no current trigger. Add a log or metric when there is an observability need.

findings.claim: The new task kwarg `assignment_source_dict` and the sender (utils/sync.py:136-144) ship in the same deploy. During a rolling deploy, an old worker receiving the kwarg raises TypeError and that assignee sync is lost.
findings.evidence: Reasoned. Sentry practice (external developer docs, not written in the repo) is to land the task parameter with a default one deploy before any caller sends it.
findings.reason: Cannot be fixed inside a single patch. It needs deploy sequencing (split the PR, or accept a transient loss window), and the release owner should decide. Unverified: settling it needs a mixed-version worker test.

findings.claim: The loop guard compares integration IDs, not external issues. A group linked to two external issues on the same integration (Jira A and B on one install) no longer propagates an inbound reassignment on A to B, which worked before the patch and was not a loop.
findings.evidence: Reasoned. sync_group_assignee_outbound queues one task per linked external issue, and should_sync returns False whenever source.integration_id == org_integration.integration_id. No test covers it.
findings.reason: This may be the intended behaviour, and with no spec it is a product-intent question. Settle it by confirming the intended semantics for multiple links on one integration, then add a test either way.

findings.claim: Measured against the inferred intent ('Breaks issue sync cycles'), status-sync cycles are not addressed; only assignee sync is protected.
findings.evidence: tasks/sync_status_outbound.py:43 is unchanged. Inbound tagging exists only in the assign/deassign paths of utils/sync.py:96-116.
findings.reason: There is no spec, so scope cannot be established. Out of this PR's evident scope; track separately if status loops are observed.
